questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a routine check-up. As part of her assessment, her high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels are measured. Her hs-CRP levels are found to be elevated. The clinician is aware of a study that examined the relationship between hs-CRP levels and the risk of myocardial infarction (MI) or stroke in women. The study divided participants into groups based on their hs-CRP levels and found a significant relationship between hs-CRP levels and the relative risk of MI/Stroke. Based on the study's findings, what can be concluded about the relationship between hs-CRP levels and the risk of MI/Stroke?

options.label: A
options.text: hs-CRP has no relation to MI/Stroke risk

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in hs-CRP decreases MI/Stroke risk

options.label: C
options.text: An increase in hs-CRP levels increases MI/Stroke risk

options.label: D
options.text: A decrease in hs-CRP levels increases MI/Stroke risk
